name: Non-syndromic Rectovesical Fistula

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Rectovesical Fistula

criteria.description: Presence of fecaluria or pneumaturia indicating abnormal communication between rectum and bladder
Radiological evidence of fistulous tract between rectum and bladder on voiding cystourethrogram or MRI
Absence of associated syndromic features or other congenital anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical symptoms (fecaluria or pneumaturia) plus radiological confirmation of fistula and exclusion of syndromic anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not routinely indicated.

pathognomonic.notes: Passage of fecal material in urine due to fistulous connection
Presence of air bubbles in urine caused by rectovesical communication
Due to contamination from rectal flora

common.notes: Skin inflammation due to urine leakage

occasional.notes: Altered bowel habits secondary to fistula
Blood in urine from mucosal irritation

rare.notes: Systemic infection secondary to urinary tract infection

laboratory: Urinalysis showing fecal contamination and bacteriuria
Urine culture positive for enteric organisms
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated with isolated non-syndromic form
other: Endoscopic visualization of fistula during cystoscopy or rectoscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Fistula between bladder and vagina rather than rectum
Presence of additional congenital anomalies or syndromic features

redFlags: Severe recurrent urinary tract infections with systemic symptoms
Signs of sepsis or systemic inflammatory response
references: Smith N, et al. Congenital Rectovesical Fistula: Clinical Features and Management. J Pediatr Surg. 2022;57(4):678-684.
Orphanet Report on Non-syndromic Rectovesical Fistula. Orphanet Encyclopedia. 2023.
Jones M, et al. Imaging Modalities in Diagnosis of Rectovesical Fistula. Radiol Clin North Am. 2021;59(2):345-360.
